messages:
dave: Quick question — I'm converting from a 1099 contractor to full-time next Monday. For my old company's 401(k), can I roll that into Redwood's plan? Do I need to fill anything with payroll or benefits, and will my HSA pre-tax election carry over or do I need to re-enroll? cc @maria :wave:

maria (People Ops): Congrats on the move! :tada: Short answers: yes you can roll into our 401(k) and you need to submit the rollover paperwork; HSA elections do NOT auto-carry — you must enroll during your new-employee window. I'll outline next steps below.

ben (Payroll): A couple of practical notes: 1) For 401(k) rollins, timeline doesn't affect payroll deductions — once you're on payroll your elective deferrals start on the first applicable paycheck per your enrollment. 2) HSA pre-tax via payroll must be elected in Workday before the payroll cutoff. Cutoff is typically the 5th of the month at 23:59 PT for the following month's payroll cycle. If you miss it, the earliest is the next cycle.

lisa (Benefits): Rollover process we accept: trustee-to-trustee or a direct rollover check made payable to the plan trustee. Please do NOT deposit an old-plan distribution into your bank and then try to contribute that amount; that can have tax implications. What we need from you: 1) a copy of the distribution form from your old plan (screenshot or PDF) 2) the old-plan rollover paperwork indicating trustee-to-trustee transfer, and 3) a completed Redwood rollover intake form (link below).

onboarding-bot: New-hire checklist updated: 401k enrollment required, HSA/FSA election window reminder sent on day 1. Link: https://hr.redwood.example/onboarding-checklist

maria (People Ops): Rollover intake form (upload to the Benefits > Documents section in Workday) — filename suggestion: "dave-401k-rollover.pdf" so it's easy to find. Our team reviews uploads within 3 business days. Email benefits@redwood.com if you need faster handling.

lisa (Benefits): HSA specifics: if you had an HSA as a contractor (rare unless you were on a W-2 with employer contributions), you can do a trustee-to-trustee transfer to our HSA custodian. If you only contributed post-tax to an HSA-like account, we can advise on the safest approach; DM me your custodian name. Note on FSA: flexible spending accounts typically don't transfer between employers — check your old plan's grace/rollover rules.

dave: Perfect, thanks everyone. I'll upload the distribution PDF to Workday today and DM @lisa the custodian name. One quick follow-up — will rolling in affect my company match timing?

ben (Payroll): Good Q — match is calculated on eligible deferrals from your start date forward. Past balances you roll in do NOT retroactively increase match. In other words, match applies to future contributions only.

maria (People Ops): Yep — same as Ben said. If you want, once you upload the docs I'll confirm receipt and give an estimated completion date. :+1:

dave: Awesome, uploading now. Thanks all!
